newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-Soviet dissident Kopelev dies in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet dissident Kopelev dies in Germany.

text.p: The former Soviet dissident and human rights campaigner Lev Kopelev has died in Germany aged 85 after a long battle with heart disease, his publisher Hoffmann und Campe said on Wednesday.

Kopelev served nearly 10 years of hard labour in Stalin's Gulag camps and prisons for showing "bourgeous-humanistic sympathy with the enemy after speaking out against the atrocities committed by Soviet troops as they marched into Germany in 1945.

He was rehabilitated in 1956, and wrote many political texts and articles in the 1960s and 1970s, when he actively supported Soviet dissidents such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn and Nobel peace prize laureate Andrei Sakharov.
He emigrated to Germany after receiving permission from Moscow to travel to the West in 1980, and was stripped of his Soviet citizenship a year later.

Kopelev, who had studied German language and literature before the war and later write a biography of playwright Berthold Brecht and a history of German theatre, settled in Cologne. He became a close friend of the German writer and Nobel prize-winner Heinrich Boell, who also lived in the city.
In 1981 Kopelev received the prestigious Peace Prize of the German Book Trade, an award that recognises literary commitment to higher ideals.
Even after the end of Soviet communism until shortly before his death, Kopelev was tireless in probing the democratic credentials of leading Russian politicians when they came to Germany.
Kopelev was born in the Ukrainian capital of Kiev in 1912. National ARD television reported that he wanted his ashes buried in Russia.
